title: Carry accepted corrections into retries of failed jobs
summary: When the user says "try again on <failed job>", the retry's reader brief must carry that job's accepted corrections, as it does for rejected jobs. I found no failed-only branch that drops corrections in carry/earlier_attempt/reader_brief. So the producer must reproduce the loss with a failed-job test and fix wherever it appears; likely suspects are retry chains and failed jobs with no verification record.

defaults_applied.how: Add failing-first tests for the failed-job case; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Limit the change to the carry path for failed-job retries.
Recovered the retry flow from reading.rs and briefs.rs instead of asking.
Test fixtures use synthetic text and redacted tokens only.
Behavior criteria are checked with cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.

assumptions: The loss happens in the brief-building path (reading.rs earlier_attempt/carry, or briefs.rs reader_brief), not in record storage.
A failed job's corrections can be lost when the failed job is itself a retry (its corrections, or its predecessors', are not carried through the chain), or when it has no verification record.
Only the reader brief for the retry needs the corrections; the producer and verifier briefs are unchanged.
Carried corrections stay redacted and quoted as data, as today.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs builds a failed job (Failed outcome) that has a final reading and accepted corrections, and asserts earlier_attempt carries them in order and redacted.
A test covers a failed job that has corrections but no verification record, and one that is itself a retry, and asserts its corrections reach the EarlierAttempt.
The reader brief for a failed earlier attempt lists the corrections under the existing corrections heading, with a briefs.rs test asserting this.
Run `cargo test` from the repository root: all tests pass, including the new failed-job correction tests.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.

out_of_scope: Changing how corrections are recorded or scored.
Changing which job states can be retried.
Any change to governance, CI, or configuration files.
departures: None beyond the reference forecast. The root cause is not located by reading alone, which slightly lowers acceptance.
